subject: 40B Development Appeals and Water Infrastructure Funding
overview: The Council approved the reprogramming of $855,000 for water and sewer infrastructure, including a flooding study for Bowen Avenue, and debated the city's strategy for appealing 40B housing developments. The body also supported state legislation to cap third-party restaurant delivery fees and finalized committee reports regarding the city's marijuana ordinance.

items.title: Water and Sewer Capital Project Reprogramming
items.summary: Approved the reprogramming of $855,000 from leak detection accounts to fund a hydraulic study for Bowen Avenue flooding, water meter replacements, and hydrant maintenance. The Council also requested updates on catch basin repairs and a full breakdown of the Water and Sewer Commission's funds.

items.title: Public Hearing: National Grid Grant of Location
items.summary: Approved a petition from National Grid to install approximately five feet of underground electric conduit near 19 Summit Road.

items.title: Resolutions: Anniversaries and Condolences
items.summary: Congratulated Dorothy and Frank Zizzo on their 40th wedding anniversary and expressed condolences to the family of Michael Meehan following a moment of silence.

items.title: Transfer for Zoning Consultant Services
items.summary: Approved transferring surplus funds from the videographer and legislative salary accounts to a fund designated for the Council's zoning consultant.

items.title: Update on Massport Airplane Noise Study
items.summary: Requested that the city's Massport Community Advisory Committee representatives update the Council on the FAA's commitment to study flight pattern changes identified in an MIT noise study.

items.title: Inquiry Regarding 40B Project Appeals
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting information on the cost and strategy of the city's appeal against the 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway project, as well as a long-term plan to reach the 10% affordable housing threshold. Discussion focused on the loss of municipal leverage under 40B and the balance between tax revenue from new growth and neighborhood impact.

items.title: Fiscal Year 2021 Budget Meeting Schedule
items.summary: Tabled a request to establish a budget meeting schedule until more information regarding the delivery of the budget books is available from the administration.

items.title: Restaurant Delivery Commission Caps
items.summary: Voted to support state legislation capping third-party delivery fees at 15% during the COVID-19 emergency and requested the Chamber of Commerce investigate creating a local delivery app.

items.title: Small Business Relief for Nonprofits
items.summary: Requested that the administration ensure nonprofit daycares and social service organizations can access small business relief funds being distributed by the city.

items.title: National Day of Mourning for COVID-19
items.summary: Held a moment of silence to honor the more than 100,000 Americans, including over 100 Medford nursing home residents, lost to the coronavirus.

items.title: Committee Reports and Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved Committee of the Whole reports regarding the zoning consultant scope and the proposed marijuana ordinance, and approved the minutes from the May 26 regular meeting.
